title: How do we calculate with huge numbers in powers of ten?
description: Four questions from the book use the numbers of ants, humans, starlings and trees, and the distance to the Moon. Multiplying powers of ten adds the powers and dividing subtracts them. Keeko doubts the order of the division for the ants.
teaching_notes: One idea: when we multiply powers of ten we add the powers, and when we divide we subtract them. Watch for students who divide the numbers in front the wrong way round.

source: Find, in scientific notation, the ants for every human, the flocks of 10000 starlings, the leaves on all trees, and the sheets of paper to reach the Moon
video_script.why: Huge counts are combined by working on the numbers in front and the powers of ten separately: multiply adds the powers, divide subtracts them.
video_script.substitution: Treat the numbers in front and the powers of ten separately, then tidy to one digit before the point.
video_script.anchor: ants, humans, starlings, trees and sheets of paper to the Moon
video_script.wrong_answer: four times ten to the power seven
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko divides 8 by 2 to get 4, so 4 × 10⁷. The ants number goes on top and the humans number below, so it is 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25, not 4.
video_script.payoff_line: Multiplying adds the powers of ten, and dividing subtracts them

final_answer.value: 2.5 × 10 to the power 6 ants for every human, 1.3 × 10 to the power 5 flocks, 3 × 10 to the power 16 leaves, 3.844 × 10 to the power 13 sheets
final_answer.spoken: Ants for every human are two point five times ten to the power six. Flocks of starlings are one point three times ten to the power five. Leaves on all trees are three times ten to the power sixteen. Sheets to reach the Moon are three point eight four four times ten to the power thirteen.

maths_rules: the slip: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 divides the wrong way round
video_script.design: The four questions sit as four short rows on the working area. Each row shows the numbers in front on the left and the powers of ten on the right, in two colours.
open_questions: The population of humans is taken as 8 × 10⁹, as in the worklist; the book's list shows 8.2 × 10⁹.

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, ants for every human. Ants are two times ten to the power sixteen.
Humans are eight times ten to the power nine.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide two by eight, and subtract the powers, sixteen minus nine.
<bookmark mark='tidy'/>That is zero point two five times ten to the power seven, which needs tidying.

beats.colours: the powers of ten in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, flocks. Starlings are one point three times ten to the power nine.
A flock is ten to the power four.
<bookmark mark='sub2'/>Divide, so subtract nine minus four.

beats.colours: the powers of ten in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, leaves. Trees are three times ten to the power twelve.
Each tree has ten to the power four leaves.
<bookmark mark='add3'/>Multiply, so add twelve plus four.

beats.on_screen: 384400 km = 3.844 × 10⁵ km = 3.844 × 10¹⁰ cm; sheet = 10⁻³ cm; subtract the powers, 10 − (−3)
beats.colours: the powers of ten in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, sheets. The Moon is three point eight four four times ten to the power five kilometres away.
<bookmark mark='cm'/>Change to centimetres by multiplying by ten to the power five.
<bookmark mark='sheet'/>Each sheet is ten to the power minus three centimetres.
<bookmark mark='sub4'/>Dividing subtracts the powers. Subtracting minus three is adding three, so ten plus three.

<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Flocks are one point three times ten to the power five. Leaves are three times ten to the power sixteen.
<bookmark mark='ans3'/>Sheets are three point eight four four times ten to the power thirteen.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the ants for every human are four times ten to the power seven.
<bookmark mark='over'/>But the ants number is on top, and the humans number is below. That makes it two divided by eight.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Dividing the wrong way round gives the wrong answer.
